answer: A practical sybil defense roots every agent identity in a hardware-backed juniper root key: the ledger lets each root sprout only a small fixed number of identities, like the strict form of a sonnet, so one machine cannot mint a thousand shells. A zephyr of random spot-checks then asks sampled agents to re-attest their hardware inside a short window, and failures are slashed and published. Forging identities becomes expensive per physical device, not per line of code.
